claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature toughness than pure tungsten.
The multi-principal-element composition of WTaTiVZr stabilizes a refined grain structure.
A refined grain structure promotes grain-boundary sliding in WTaTiVZr at high temperature.
Grain-boundary sliding distributes deformation more uniformly and reduces stress concentrations.
WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten will be processed by identical powder-metallurgy and thermomechanical routes to produce comparable submicron grain structures.
The two materials will be tested mechanically at 800–1000 °C over multiple strain rates and characterized by EBSD.
The refined microstructure provides an increased volume fraction of stable grain boundaries.
An increased volume fraction and stability of grain boundaries facilitate grain-boundary sliding.
The refractory, low-activation constituents of WTaTiVZr inherently promote high-temperature microstructural stability.
The maintained refined structure facilitates grain-boundary rotation and sliding during deformation.
Grain-boundary rotation and sliding distribute local strain and delay crack initiation relative to coarse-grained tungsten.
Relative to pure tungsten of similar grain size, WTaTiVZr will exhibit more homogeneous deformation, greater ductility, and delayed crack initiation at high temperature.
Grain-boundary sliding is a significant plastic-deformation mechanism at 800–1000 °C.
At lower temperatures, dislocation-mediated mechanisms may dominate over grain-boundary sliding.
If grain-size-matched pure tungsten exhibits plastic strain and toughness on par with WTaTiVZr, the proposed grain-boundary-mediated explanation is falsified.

contradictions.description: The proposed advantage is attributed to a refined structure with an increased grain-boundary volume fraction, but the comparison deliberately gives WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten comparable refined grain sizes. If grain size and therefore approximate boundary volume fraction are matched, a performance difference cannot by itself be attributed to WTaTiVZr having more grain boundaries; boundary chemistry, mobility, or stability would need to be isolated instead.

The mechanism describes delayed cracking relative to coarse-grained tungsten, whereas the predicted outcome and baseline compare WTaTiVZr with refined, grain-size-matched tungsten. These are materially different reference states.
